title: Origin of Long-Lived Nuclear Spin States and Coherences in Aliphatic Chains Revealed by Relaxation Theory
authors: Danil A. Markelov, Kirill F. Sheberstov
abstract: Delocalized long-lived states (LLSs) and collective zero-quantum long-lived coherences (LLCs) in aliphatic chains provide a promising route for preserving nuclear spin order with lifetimes that exceed the conventional $T_1$ and $T_2$ relaxation times, respectively. Their extended lifetimes make them attractive for applications including hyperpolarization storage, ligand-observed drug screening based on the loss of longevity upon binding to a target protein, and quantum information processing exploiting the collective properties of many-body spin systems. Although LLSs and LLCs have been observed experimentally in methylene networks, their origin and general structure in chains of arbitrary length have remained unclear. Here we show that these relaxation-protected modes follow directly from Redfield relaxation theory. Specifically, we construct the long-lived subspace, i.e., the zero-eigenvalue subspace of the relaxation superoperator associated with the dominant intra-pair dipole--dipole relaxation mechanism. The long-lived subspace contains $2^N-1$ independent non-trivial operators, which excludes the identity operator, where $N>1$ is the number of $-\mathrm{CH}_2-$ groups in the chain. In achiral molecules, conservation of the global intra-pair permutation parity restricts experimental access to at most $2^N-2$ of these operators, whereas in chiral molecules this parity is not conserved, making up to $2^N-1$ long-lived operators accessible. We further develop a general framework for constructing both LLSs and LLCs in aliphatic chains containing an arbitrary number of $-\mathrm{CH}_2-$ groups in achiral molecules, and illustrate the approach explicitly for chains with $N=2$, 3, and 4 methylene groups.
summary: The paper theoretically derives the existence and structure of long-lived nuclear spin states and coherences in aliphatic chains using Redfield relaxation theory. By identifying operators annihilated by the dominant dipole–dipole interaction, it provides a general framework to predict these protected quantum modes. This is crucial for applications ranging from hyperpolarization storage to quantum information processing.
main_problem: The primary goal is determining the fundamental origin and general structure of delocalized long-lived states (LLSs) and collective zero-quantum long-lived coherences (LLCs) in aliphatic spin chains.
main_result: These protected modes are shown to arise directly from Redfield relaxation theory by finding operators annihilated by the dominant intra-pair dipole–dipole relaxation superoperator. The accessible number of such independent non-trivial operators depends on molecular chirality.
method: The authors employ Redfield relaxation theory, constructing and analyzing the zero-eigenvalue subspace of the relaxation superoperator associated with the intra-pair dipole–dipole interaction.
model_or_system: The system is an aliphatic spin chain composed of $N$ methylene groups ($-	ext{CH}_2-$). The analysis uses spin operators for pairs of spins and models the dynamics via the relaxation superoperator $\hat{\mathcal{R}}_{\text{intra}}$.
key_observables: Long-lived states (LLSs) and long-lived coherences (LLCs), which are characterized by their extended lifetimes exceeding conventional $T_1$ and $T_2$ times.
important_parameters: The number of methylene groups, $N$; the nature of the molecule (achiral vs. chiral); and the dominant relaxation mechanism (intra-pair dipole–dipole interaction).
main_assumptions: Cross-correlations between different dipole–dipole interaction sites are neglected due to rapid averaging from fast molecular rotation.
figures_summary: Figures schematically illustrate the local LLO subspace, the construction of collective LLOs via product operators ($\prod \hat{P}(X)$), and the classification of these products into parity-defined subspaces ($P(MT)$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the physical problem (LLSs/LLCs) to applying Redfield theory, deriving the mathematical condition for protection ($\hat{\mathcal{T}}^{(2)}_{2,m} \hat{L} = 0$), establishing the combinatorial structure of the zero-eigenvalue space ($2^N-1$ operators), and finally developing explicit construction methods using population projectors.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical framework linking fundamental relaxation theory (Redfield) to observable quantum phenomena (LLCs/LLSs) in molecular spin systems, which is highly relevant for understanding coherence preservation in complex biological or chemical environments.

(b) An operator corresponding to an LLO in an aliphatic spin chain containing N −CH2−groups is constructed as a product of either ˆP(S0) or ˆP(T) within each group. (c) These products are classified according to the number of triplet populations T they contain, thereby defining the triplet-number subspaces P(MT).
